verdict.rationale: Bruno ships an official, documented CLI (bru) that runs API collections from the command line. It outputs JSON, JUnit and HTML reports, supports runtime flags such as --global-env-var and --sandbox=developer, and has official Docker images for CI/CD and local runs. That makes it scriptable by agents, and the site says collections work with Git, your IDE, and your agents. Missing for 10: documentation of agent-specific CLI workflows (e.g., agents invoking bru directly), and independent or hands-on corroboration of CLI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: With Bruno CLI, you can run your API collections with ease using simple command line commands.
Official Docker images for the Bruno CLI let you run API collections in CI/CD pipelines and locally without installing Node.js or npm on the host.
Easily create reports in multiple formats, including JSON, JUnit, and HTML, to analyze and share test results.
add --global-env-var to override global environment variables at runtime
Collections stored as code. Works with Git, your IDE, and your agents.
